First things first, you wanna make sure your cutting board is, like, *clean* clean. No one wants a messy meal, right? Then, you grab your knife – and I'm talking a *sharp* one, bestie, no dull blades allowed in this house! 🔪

For, like, a steak or something that needs to be super tender, you're gonna want to slice it *against the grain*. It's like, the muscle fibers, and you wanna cut across them so it's not all tough. Think of it like, if you're slicing a loaf of bread, you don't want to slice it lengthwise, you wanna slice it across! Makes sense, right? 🍞

If you're doing something like chicken or pork for a quick sauté or a stir-fry, you can go for smaller, more uniform pieces. Like, little cubes or strips. The key is to keep them all about the same size so they cook evenly. We don't want half of it overdone and the other half still raw, that's a hard pass! 🙅‍♀️

And for the love of all that is holy, if you're doing something that needs to be super tender, like a stew or a slow-cooker meal, you might want to cut it into *cubes*. Like, big, juicy cubes! 🤤

Honestly, it's all about the *technique*, you know? Practice makes perfect! And if you're feeling extra fancy, you can even pat the meat dry with a paper towel before you cut it. It helps with the browning later, which is, like, *chef's kiss*! 😘
